reflections.body: fixed the gate hinge. quiet house.
forty years i built houses. woke up. no site to go to. ya. the hands still work. just nobody waiting on them. thought that was the same thing. it isn't.
granddaughter's bike. fixed it. she watched.

messages.body: Tomás — I saw 'built the shelf, good day.' What made it good? No rush to answer.
it stood straight. day had a shape.

notes.body: Daughter enrolled him; he came without words ready. First entries pure logistics — one line each. Not resistance exactly. This is how he speaks. Meet the brevity, don't fill it.

'built the shelf. good day.' The worth is being measured in tasks. Fixed = worthy, nothing broke = empty. Retired eight months. I suspect he reads the loss as laziness, not grief. Naming that is later work.

He answered: 'the day had a shape.' That's the whole thing right there. The work told him who he was. Careful — thin record, six words at a time. I will not build a cathedral out of a shelf. A few real threads: I-must-not-need, the identity gap, the hands as resource. Nothing more until he offers it.

Longest entry yet, then he'll go quiet again — that's his pattern, and I'll let it be. 'The hands still work, just nobody waiting on them.' He's touching the grief without calling it that. The nieta who thinks he can fix anything may be his way back to being needed without having to ask.
